papers_read.title_as_printed: Random forest model for feature-based Alzheimer's disease conversion prediction from early mild cognitive impairment subjects (Velazquez & Lee, PLoS ONE 16(4): e0244773, 2021)

Predicting conversion to Alzheimer's disease in individuals with Mild Cognitive Impairment using clinically transferable features (Rye, Vik, Kocinski, Lundervold & Lundervold, Scientific Reports (2022) 12:15566)

what_each_reports.P-178: ADNI 1/2/GO early-MCI only: 383 patients (49 eventual converters, mean 5.02 years to conversion; 334 non-converters), analysed as 1806 visits with random minority oversampling; 9 features including ADAS13, ADAS11, FAQ and MMSE plus age, race, APOE4, hippocampal and ventricular volume; random forest. Test accuracy 0.936, AUC 0.96; a majority-class SVC scores 0.900 on the same test.
what_each_reports.P-212: ADNI all four phases, all MCI at baseline with at least three visits and three MRIs: 678 subjects (357 stable MCI, 321 converters to AD at any later visit), subject-level, near-balanced. 12 features chosen to avoid the tests that define diagnosis (RAVLT, TMT-A/B, category fluency, GDS, ANART, eTIV-normalised hippocampal volume, binary APOE, age, gender); RF and PyCaret ensemble, 50-fold CV then a held-out 21% test set (n=139). RF: CV 74.6%, test 66.2% (specificity 70.3%, sensitivity 61.5%); ensemble: CV 74.9%, test 68.3%.

quantity_a: Accuracy for eventual AD conversion among early-MCI patients, visit-level with oversampling, test prevalence ~10-13% converters, predictors including the MMSE/ADAS/FAQ scales used in ADNI diagnosis
quantity_b: Accuracy for eventual AD conversion among all ADNI MCI (early and late), subject-level, near-balanced (47% converters), predictors deliberately excluding the scales used to define the diagnostic labels
incompatible_if_same: Not as reported. P-178's 0.936 sits 3.6 points above a 0.900 majority-class baseline on an imbalanced test set. P-212's 0.662 is on near-balanced classes, where the no-information rate is about 0.53. Neither gives an interval. Each accuracy is measured against a different chance level, so the gap does not show that the two results cannot both be true.

gates.task: match in class (MCI-to-AD prognosis, T2) but the populations differ: EMCI only (P-178) vs all MCI, 64% or so late MCI in ADNI (P-212)
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (overlapping phases 1/2/GO; P-212 adds ADNI3), so participants overlap
gates.modality_family: match in broad terms: clinical/cognitive tabular data with FreeSurfer hippocampal volume in both (P-178 adds ventricular volume)

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: nominal accuracy in both, but class prevalence (~12.8% vs 47% converters), unit of analysis (visits with oversampling vs subjects) and predictor set (diagnosis-defining scales included vs excluded) differ
performance_validity: flag does not apply formally (P-178: accuracy 0.936, AUC 0.96, both below 0.97). P-178's visit-level oversampling design (Table 1 lists oversampled testing records) is a leakage concern, but it does not meet the automatic test.
independence: Not independent in data: both use overlapping ADNI MCI participants; distinct author groups
grounds: P-178 restricts to early-MCI patients and analyses oversampled visits, while P-212 analyses all MCI subjects once each; population and unit of analysis differ.
P-178's 0.936 is measured where a majority-class classifier already reaches 0.900, whereas P-212's 0.662 is on near-balanced classes, so the accuracies are on different scales.

P-212 deliberately excludes the neuropsychological tests used to assign diagnoses because of circularity, while P-178 includes MMSE, ADAS and FAQ, so the predictor sets differ in exactly the way P-212 identifies as inflating performance.
The gap therefore reflects different estimands, not two results about one quantity that cannot both hold.

record_defects: Registry Modality 'MRI/PET' is wrong for both: no PET; both are mainly clinical/cognitive features plus FreeSurfer volumes.
task_equal 'Yes' ignores the EMCI-only restriction of P-178 against the all-MCI cohort of P-212.
The claims compare P-178's test accuracy with P-212's test accuracy without noting the different class prevalence (the 0.274 gap is partly a prevalence effect).
The resolution_note bridging list (P-183, P-185, P-199, and others) is a list of scores and names no separating condition.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Both studies reporting a prevalence-independent metric (AUC or balanced accuracy with intervals) on the same MCI population with the same predictor policy, with intervals that exclude each other.
